_comment: Schema contract - what import_to_egdb.py builds in the Enterprise Geodatabase.
Generated by analyze_source.py from the source named below; safe to edit by hand,
which is the point: every field carries the measurement its type was chosen from,
so disagreeing with the inference does not mean re-reading the data.
Types are ArcGIS field types, not PostgreSQL ones. An Enterprise Geodatabase has
no boolean type, so a boolean column appears here as SHORT with the substitution
recorded in its evidence block rather than applied silently.

generated.types_from: measurement, because the source declares no schema

spatial_reference.decided_by: column names latitude/longitude: a geographic pair is decimal degrees, EPSG:4326. Note that 'decimal degrees' and 'EPSG:3857' are mutually exclusive - EPSG:3857 is metres.
spatial_reference.note: A feature class holds exactly one spatial reference, and creating it with the wrong one does not error at write time - the coordinates are simply interpreted as the wrong grid. Only a bounding-box check notices.

geometry.note: x_column feeds the easting/longitude and y_column the northing/latitude. The contract names them separately rather than as a pair so that an axis swap is a visible edit rather than an ordering assumption.

name_limits.note: Enterprise geodatabase limits, tighter than PostgreSQL's own 63 characters. ArcGIS does not delimit object names, so a name that would need quoting - mixed case, a space, a reserved word - is a name ArcGIS cannot address even though PostgreSQL stores it.

evidence.reason: every value is an integer literal
evidence.note: LONG regardless of the measured range. SHORT would fit here only as long as no later row exceeds it; edit the contract to SHORT deliberately if that is a constraint of the data rather than an accident of this sample.

evidence.reason: values are not uniformly boolean, numeric or ISO 8601 dates
evidence.note: TEXT length 40 = the measured maximum 21 times 1.5, rounded up to a multiple of 10. The measurement is a floor, not the answer: the next batch of data is longer.

sample: The eastern gate of an abandoned dwarven mine, sealed for nine ages.
A crumbling watchpost above the river, staffed only by crows.
A riverside archive where every book insists on being read aloud.
evidence.reason: values are not uniformly boolean, numeric or ISO 8601 dates
evidence.note: TEXT length 120 = the measured maximum 76 times 1.5, rounded up to a multiple of 10. The measurement is a floor, not the answer: the next batch of data is longer.

evidence.reason: every value is a numeric literal and at least one is decimal
evidence.note: DOUBLE, never FLOAT. A 32-bit float carries about 7 significant decimal digits, which silently rounds a 5-decimal latitude or an EPSG:3857 metre value - a plausible-looking coordinate in the wrong place.
